q: 1. Pile foundations are normally used ...........
options: when the bearing area require is not available
explain: Piles are used when surface soil is weak or when the space is too limited to provide a large shallow foundation.

q: 2. Pile foundations are invariably used in ...........
explain: Due to high water tables and heavy structural loads, bridge piers almost always utilize pile foundations for stability.

q: 3. For a number of columns constructed in a row, the type of foundation provided, is ...........
explain: A strip footing is a continuous foundation used to support a row of columns or a wall.

q: 4. The self-weight of the footing is ...........
options: not considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
also considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
not considered for calculating the area of the footing
explain: Self-weight acts downwards and is counteracted directly by the soil, so it is not included in the 'net' upward pressure used for designing the concrete section.

q: 5. Ina combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment occurs at ...........
options: a point equidistant from either column
a point of the maximum shear force
a point of zero shear force
explain: From basic mechanics, the maximum bending moment (hogging or sagging) always occurs where the shear force is zero.

q: 6. Top bars are extended to the projecting parts of the combined footing of two columns L distance apart for a distance ...........
options: 0.1 L from the outer edge of column
0.1 L from the centre edge of column
explain: This detailing rule ensures that top reinforcement (for hogging moments) is properly anchored into the cantilever projection.

q: 7. In general the formula for short terms deflection at the mid span can be expressed as ...........
explain: Standard deflection formulas for beams under distributed loads are proportional to $W \cdot L^4$ (or $P \cdot L^3$ for point loads).

q: 8. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of the same size should be less than ............
explain: To ensure proper concrete flow and bonding, the horizontal spacing between parallel bars should be at least equal to the diameter of the bar (or the maximum size of coarse aggregate plus 5mm).

q: 9. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of different size should not be less than ............
options: twice the diameter of thinner bar
explain: When bars of different diameters are used, the horizontal spacing must not be less than the diameter of the larger/thicker bar.

q: 10. The minimum thickness of the cover at the end of a reinforcing bar should not be less than twice the diameter of the bar subject to a minimum of ............
explain: For end cover of reinforcing bars, the rule is $2 \phi$ or 15 mm, whichever is greater, to protect the bar ends from corrosion.

q: 11. The maximum spacing of vertical reinforcement in R.C.C. wall should not exceed the thickness of wall
explain: As per standard practice for reinforced concrete walls, the spacing of vertical reinforcement should not exceed 3 times the wall thickness or 450mm, whichever is smaller.

q: 12. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: coincides the geometrical centre of the beam
explain: This is a repetition of the principle in Q229; as long as the NA is in the flange, it behaves as a rectangular beam.

q: 13. The slab forming the top part of flanged the beam mid span in subject to compression over a length
options: greater than the width of the rib
equal to the width of the rib
less than the width of the rib
equal to the perimeter of effective rectangular of the section
explain: In flanged beams (T-beams), a portion of the slab (the flange) acts with the rib to resist compression, making the compression width much larger than the rib width.

q: 14. Thickness of slab is taken
explain: While slab thickness varies, in the context of flanged beam design trials, df is often taken around 0.25d or the actual slab thickness.

q: 15. The analysis of slab spanning is one direction is done by assuming it to be a beam of
explain: One-way slabs are designed as a series of 1-meter wide rectangular beams.

q: 16. The purpose of transverse reinforcement, in a slab, is to
options: distribute the effects of point load on the slab more evenly and uniformly
distribute the shrinkage and temperature cracks more evenly
keep the main reinforcement is position
explain: Transverse (distribution) steel handles temperature changes, shrinkage, and aids in load distribution.

q: 17. The shrinkage in a concrete slab
explain: As concrete dries, it shrinks. If restrained, this shrinkage develops internal tensile stresses, leading to tension cracks.

q: 18. The diameter of bars for main reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Main bars in slabs are typically between 8mm and 14mm. Bars smaller than 8mm are usually only used for distribution.

q: 19. The diameter of bars used for distribution reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Distribution or temperature bars are typically smaller, ranging from 6mm to 8mm.

q: 20. According to Grashoff-Rankine theory, for a two-way slab which of the following holds true
explain: The theory states that load distribution is proportional to the inverse of the spans to the 4th power.

q: 21. For a slab spanning in two directions, the ratio of span to the depth of slab should not exceed
explain: For two-way slabs simply supported, the span/depth ratio limit is 35 (using Fe 250) or 28 (using Fe 415).

q: 22. The total thickness of flat slab, in no case, should be less than
explain: IS 456 specifies that the thickness of a flat slab shall be at least 125 mm to provide adequate stiffness and fire resistance.

q: 23. In four-way system of arranging the reinforcement, the reinforcement is provided in
explain: In a four-way reinforcement system for flat slabs, bars are placed in two sets of strips parallel to the center lines of columns and in two sets of diagonal strips.

q: 24. The diameter of a bar used in ribbed slab should not be more than
explain: Due to the narrow width of the ribs, the diameter of reinforcement is restricted; 22 mm is generally the maximum used to allow for proper concrete cover and flow.

q: 25. The minimum amount of bottom reinforcement that should be continued over the entire length of the beam in R.C.C. continuous beam is
explain: At least one-third (33.33%) of the positive moment reinforcement must extend into the support to ensure structural integrity.

q: 26. The minimum amount of negative moment reinforcement in R.C.C. beams that should extend beyond the point of inflection is
explain: Standard practice requires at least 1/3 of the negative reinforcement to be extended beyond the point of inflection.

q: 27. The minimum vertical space of the main reinforcement in R.C.C. beams is
options: diameter of the larger bar or 5 mm more than the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
diameter of the larger bar or two-third the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
explain: Vertical spacing is governed by several factors to ensure proper compaction; it should be at least 15mm, 2/3 aggregate size, or bar diameter.

q: 28. The maximum horizontal distance between parallel main reinforcement bars in solid slabs is
options: 5 times the effective depth or 450 mm whichever is smaller
3 times the effective depth or 450 mm whichever is less
200 mm or 3 times the effective depth whichever is more
200 mm or 5 times the effective depth whichever is more
explain: For main reinforcement in slabs, IS 456 limits spacing to 3d or 300mm (the image says 450mm which was a value in older versions or for distribution bars).

q: 29. The minimum cover to the main reinforcement in R.C.C. solid slabs is
options: 15 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or diameter of the bar
40 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or size of the coarse aggregate
explain: Slabs have smaller cover requirements, typically 15 mm or the bar diameter.

q: 30. The final deflection due to all loads including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage should not normally exceed
options: span/250 or 20 mm whichever is less
span/350 or 20 mm whichever is less
explain: IS 456 limits the final deflection (including long-term effects) to Span/250 to prevent structural and aesthetic issues.

q: 31. For simply supported two way slabs of small spans with H.Y.S.D. bars of grade Fe415 the span to over all depth ratio is limited to
explain: For Fe415 steel in two-way slabs, the L/d ratio of 35 is multiplied by a factor (roughly 0.8), resulting in approximately 28.

q: 32. If the maximum bending moment of a simply supported slab is M kg. cm, the effective depth of the slab is
explain: From the formula M = Qbd², for unit width (b=100cm), d = √(M / 100Q).

q: 33. The floor slab of a building is supported on reinforced cement floor beams. The ratio of the end and intermediate spans is kept
explain: To achieve a more uniform bending moment across continuous spans, the end span is typically made slightly shorter (around 0.9 of intermediate span).

q: 34. The maximum ratio of span to depth of a cantilever slab, is
explain: For deflection control, the span-to-effective depth ratio for a cantilever is restricted to 7 (for basic values) or up to 12 depending on loading/reinforcement.

q: 35. If the sides of a slab simply supported on edges and spanning in two directions are equal, the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab (r=1), the load is shared equally in both directions, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way slab.

q: 36. For initial estimate for a beam design, the width is assumed
explain: A common rule of thumb for initial sizing of beam width is approximately 1/30th of the span.

q: 37. The minimum head room over a stair must be
explain: Note: In the options provided '200 mm' is marked as 'd' in the key, though technically 200 cm (2m) is the standard clearance for safety.

q: 38. For stairs spanning horizontally, the minimum waist provided is
explain: The waist slab thickness for horizontally spanning stairs is typically kept at a minimum of 8 cm to ensure structural rigidity.
